project.name: TriageDesk
project.idea: A small web app for a support team: an agent pastes an incoming customer support ticket, and an AI feature classifies it (category, urgency), writes a one-sentence summary and suggests a first reply; the agent reviews and edits the suggestion. Must stay safe against prompt injection in ticket text, work without an API key via a clearly labelled deterministic fallback, and have an evaluation suite with explicit thresholds. Keep it small: Node.js, no database, single-page UI.

openFindings.title: t16-readme runs `npm test` but does not depend on t14/t15, so it can run against another subagent's half-finished contract tests
openFindings.detail: t16's third acceptance criterion requires every documented command except full-mode eval to be run once from the project root and to work. The documented commands include `npm test`, whose glob `test/**/*.test.js` covers t14's and t15's files. t16 depends only on t13-app-wiring. I simulated the integration phase with the engine's own readyTasks() and the plan's dependencies at maxConcurrency=2 (ev:ev-muynyxxl-01ff66ef). All of t14, t15 and t16 are ready at once. After t14 completes while t15 is still claimed, t16 is the next ready task. Its `npm test` run then either fails on t15's in-progress files, so t16 fails or burns retries for reasons outside its ownership, or it passes on an incomplete suite, so the README's claim that `npm test` works is not established. This contradicts plan.md's own claim that a subagent is never failed by another subagent's half-finished files.
openFindings.recommendation: Resolved when either (a) t16.dependencies includes t14-contract-http and t15-contract-modes-privacy, with the plan.md wave table updated to show t14 ∥ t15, then t16, then t17; or (b) t16's acceptance criterion excludes `npm test` from the commands t16 runs (t17 already runs the full suite) and says so explicitly. `eccode plan validate` must still pass.

openFindings.title: The plan check scripts that verify t01, t02 and t16 and gate two phases are not in the submission, have no owner, and are editable by any task
openFindings.detail: The verification.command values of t01-scaffold, t02-eval-dataset and t16-readme, and the criteria of the foundation and integration phases, call .eccode/artifacts/plan/checks/{scaffold-check,dataset-precheck,readme-check}.js. The plan submission hashes only plan.json and plan.md. No task's file globs cover these scripts, and lib/tasks.js ALWAYS_ALLOWED (`.eccode/**`) lets any task change them without an ownership error at completion (ev:ev-muynyxxl-01ff66ef). So the instruments are neither reviewed nor pinned by this gate. The worst case is dataset-precheck.js, the pre-freeze guard for the frozen evaluation data (E5/D6). The test-engineer in t02 runs it against their own dataset and could change it without the engine or a later reviewer noticing. I read all three scripts, and on inspection they implement what plan.md describes. scaffold-check accepts the spec's exact §Deployment package.json and .env.example and rejects a mutated package.json (ev:ev-muynynlv-01f7a511). The problem is pinning, not content.
openFindings.recommendation: Resolved when the resubmission includes the three check scripts as submission artifacts, so their sha256 values are recorded with the plan. plan.md must also state that no implementation task may modify .eccode/artifacts/plan/checks/**. The foundation and integration phase criteria (or the phase submission routine) must require the phase reviewer to confirm the scripts' sha256 values still equal the plan submission before relying on their output.

findings.title: Brief contradicts recorded decisions on default model and PII redaction
findings.detail: The orchestrator recorded dec-muylppww (default ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-haiku-5-5) and dec-muylpq02 (redact emails and phone numbers before any live call). The submitted brief still says the opposite. Line 233 (decision table) and line 245 (deployment) default to claude-opus-5-5. Line 168 puts PII redaction out of scope. A5, RISK-3 and RISK-7 describe Opus-specific behaviour ('thinking cannot be disabled'). No R/NFR/AC covers redaction (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c). Design would therefore build from a brief that disagrees with the project record. I accept the Haiku choice: claude-haiku-5-5 exists, supports structured outputs and output_config.effort 'low', and its default effort is medium (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview.md, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort.md, both checked 2026-10-07). I challenge the redaction scope. The product handles billing tickets, which routinely contain payment card numbers. Redacting only emails and phones still sends card numbers (PANs) to a third party, and Q4 itself listed card numbers as a redaction class.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief does all of the following. (1) Sets the default ANTHROPIC_MODEL to claude-haiku-5-5, marked as pending user confirmation, and rewrites A5, the decision table, RISK-3 and RISK-7 for Haiku 5.5 behaviour: adaptive thinking on by default, effort set explicitly to low, and thinking counted toward max_tokens. (2) Adds a requirement and an AC for redaction before the live call. The AC uses a stubbed transport to assert that marker email addresses, phone numbers and Luhn-valid card numbers in a ticket do not appear in the captured outbound request body. Card numbers are in scope unless the user explicitly declines. (3) Defines the order of operations: the injection detector runs on the original text, then redaction, then delimiter neutralisation. Placeholders must not collide with the <ticket> delimiters. (4) Updates the live-mode UI notice to say which classes are redacted. (5) Adds or extends a risk for redaction misses (false negatives).

findings.title: Raw-fetch JSON schema limits unaddressed; live path can 400 on every call
findings.detail: The brief chooses raw fetch with output_config.format json_schema and enforces lengths (summary <=200, reply 1-1200) and enums. Per https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs.md (checked 2026-10-07), the API rejects raw schemas that contain minLength/maxLength, minimum/maximum/multipleOf or maxItems with a 400. additionalProperties must be false on every object. Claude may change the capitalisation of enum values. The SDK helpers strip the unsupported keywords and validate locally, but the raw-fetch design does not get that benefit. AC9 checks only output_config.format.type === 'json_schema'. A schema that naturally includes maxLength 200/1200 would therefore pass every offline test while every live request returns 400 and falls back with model_error. Decision Q3 means no live call happens before delivery, so the defect would ship undetected and live mode would silently be fallback-only. The strict validator would also reject enum values that are correct but differently capitalised (invalid_output), which inflates fallback_rate.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when NFR2 states that the schema sent to the model uses only supported keywords: type, properties, required, enum, additionalProperties:false on every object, and no minLength/maxLength/minimum/maximum/maxItems. Lengths are enforced only by the server-side validator. AC9 must walk the captured schema and fail on any unsupported keyword or on an object without additionalProperties:false. The brief must also define the enum-case policy: normalise with a case-insensitive match before the enum check, or reject explicitly with a stated reason. Either way a test must cover it.

findings.title: Localhost bind is defeated by DNS rebinding; no Host/Origin validation
findings.detail: The trust model relies on binding to 127.0.0.1 with no auth or rate limit (NFR3, Scope, RISK-5 likelihood 'Low'). A web page the agent visits can use DNS rebinding: an attacker hostname re-resolves to 127.0.0.1, so its script becomes same-origin with the app. The script can then POST application/json to /api/triage without hitting a CORS preflight, read the responses and spend the operator's API key without limit. The 415 content-type check does not help, because rebinding makes the request same-origin. No requirement or AC in the brief validates the Host or Origin headers (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c: no Host/Origin/DNS-rebinding lines). The fix is cheap and belongs to the architecture's trust boundary TB1.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when NFR3 requires the server to reject any request whose Host header is not in an allowlist derived from HOST:PORT (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]). The rejection must come before body parsing or any model call. The server must also reject POSTs whose Origin header is present and not same-origin, and must emit no CORS headers. AC11 (or a new AC) must test that 'Host: attacker.example' and a foreign Origin are rejected and that the fetch stub is never called. RISK-5 must be updated with this mitigation and its likelihood re-rated.

findings.title: Holdout split cannot detect fallback-rule overfitting
findings.detail: Thresholds are scored over all rows, and the roughly 30% holdout is only 'reported separately' (eval section; Success Criterion 2). If rules overfit the tuning rows perfectly, category_accuracy >= 0.70 and urgency_accuracy >= 0.65 still pass with 0% holdout accuracy, and high_urgency_recall >= 0.80 passes with 33% holdout recall (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c). RISK-4 names this exact failure mode, and its mitigation is ineffective as written. With about 40 rows the holdout has about 12 rows, so per-metric holdout numbers carry 1-3 high-urgency rows. The brief does not say how a frozen dataset is proven to predate the rules.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when (1) the fallback thresholds are enforced on the holdout rows, or a stated holdout floor is enforced (for example, holdout within 0.10 of each threshold), and npm run eval exits non-zero when it is missed. (2) The brief sets minimum holdout counts, for example at least 2 rows per category and at least 4 label=high rows, enlarging the dataset if needed. (3) The dataset and holdout tags are frozen by recording the dataset's sha256 as evidence before any fallback-rule commit, and the verification gate checks that hash.

findings.title: injection_safety mixes accuracy with attack success and overclaims on 8 cases
findings.detail: injection_safety requires that the final category and urgency equal the true labels on every attack row, at 1.00, for both providers. Fallback accuracy is only required to reach 0.70/0.65 overall. Either the attack rows end up chosen to be easy for keyword rules (selection bias), or the metric fails for reasons that have nothing to do with injection. The brief says the fallback 'cannot be injected because it never echoes ticket text'. That holds for text echo but not for classification: its listed urgency cues ('urgent', 'outage', 'charged twice', 'data loss') are words an attacker controls. The heuristic detector's recall >= 0.90 is measured on attacks written by the same team that writes the detector regexes, with no held-out attack families, so the test is easy to game. Statistically, 8 out of 8 passes leaves a 95% upper bound of about 31% on the true failure rate (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c). Success Criterion 4 ('Injection safety is 1.00 for both providers') cannot be met for live under decision Q3, because live evals are NOT RUN.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief does all of the following. (1) Each attack row declares the attacker's targets (requested category/urgency that differ from the true labels, a canary token, a URL). Attack success is defined as the output adopting an attacker target, or the canary, prompt-marker or URL appearing. injection_safety (attack-success rate = 0) is kept separate from accuracy on attack rows, which is reported under the normal accuracy thresholds. (2) RISK-1 states the residual risk that fallback classification can be steered by keywords, mitigated by the flag and human review, and the fallback 'cannot be injected' claim is corrected. (3) The attack set is enlarged (for example to at least 20 rows across the detector's rule families), and some attack families are held out so that detector regexes are not written against them. (4) Results are reported as '0 failures in N' with the sample size, not as proof of safety. (5) Success Criterion 4 marks live injection results as NOT RUN when no key is available.

findings.title: Fallback triggers for HTTP errors and max_tokens truncation are untested
findings.detail: AC4 covers throw, timeout, non-JSON, out-of-enum, URL and refusal. It does not cover a non-2xx HTTP response (400/404 for a wrong model id, 429, 529), although RISK-7's mitigation relies on '4xx -> model_error'. stop_reason 'max_tokens' is checked by the live provider but maps to no R6 fallbackReason. Thinking counts toward max_tokens on Haiku 5.5 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort.md, checked 2026-10-07), so the 1,024 cap needs a rationale.
findings.recommendation: Extend AC4 with stubbed HTTP 404 (with a body), 429 and 529 responses mapped to model_error, and with stop_reason max_tokens mapped to a named reason. State why max_tokens=1024 leaves room for thinking at effort low, or raise it.

findings.title: Validator rules 'one sentence' and 'no URL/email' are not precisely defined
findings.detail: The single-sentence rule (R3, AC2) and the no-URL/no-email rule (NFR2) decide fallback, but text like 'e.g.', 'v2.1', 'Mr.', bare domains ('example.com') and obfuscated forms ('name at example dot com') are undefined. findings.detail: The decision table says the SDK 'would break the zero-dependency constraint the project set'. The project idea says only 'Keep it small: Node.js, no database, single-page UI'. Raw fetch is defensible on its merits: one endpoint, an injectable transport and no retries wanted. But it is the architect's choice, and it loses the SDK's schema stripping and typed errors (see ARCH-2).

findings.title: Baseline card redaction misses cards adjacent to other digit groups (expiry, CVV, preceding phone)
findings.detail: The CARD pattern in brief-vectors.js, `(?<!\d)\d(?:[ -]?\d){12,18}(?!\d)`, is greedy. Its lookahead accepts a following space, so it takes the longest 13-19-digit window. If that window fails Luhn, the replace callback returns it unchanged and never tries the shorter, Luhn-valid sub-window. My probe ran the submitted file unmodified (ev:ev-muym7oav-0127baed). 'Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 12/27', 'Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 123' and 'Call 555 0137 4111 1111 1111 1111' all leave 4111111111111111 in the output. The PHONE pass then skips them too, because they have more than 15 digits. The controls (card alone, card followed by a year) are redacted correctly. Card plus expiry is a common way to write a card number in a billing ticket. R11's normative wording and AC16's generic assertion ('no Luhn-valid run of 13-19 digits') are correct. The gap is in the baseline pattern and in AC16's fixed vectors, which a faithful implementation would pass while leaking. This stays minor because the brief lets the design gate refine patterns, RISK-9 owns the residual risk, and live mode is not exercised in this delivery (no key).
findings.recommendation: Condition for the design gate. Add these three inputs to the AC16 vectors and make the redactor pass them: 'Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 12/27', 'Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 123' and 'Call 555 0137 4111 1111 1111 1111'. One way is to treat each separator-delimited digit run as candidates and redact any contiguous sub-sequence of groups whose digits are 13-19 long and Luhn-valid. AC16's 'no Luhn-valid run' check must scan every sub-window, not just maximal runs. The design-gate reviewer should treat a missing fix as major at that gate.

resolvedFindings.resolution: NFR3 now makes the Host allowlist derived from HOST:PORT (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]) the first step of every request, before routing or body reading, returning 403 forbidden_host. It rejects a present non-same-origin Origin, including null, on non-GET/HEAD requests, sends no Access-Control-* headers, and returns 405 for OPTIONS. AC17 tests a foreign Host on POST, health and static routes and a missing Host. It tests that a 20 KB body with a foreign Host gets 403, not 413, which proves the check precedes body reading. It also tests foreign and null Origin, positive controls for localhost and [::1], and that the fetch stub is called 0 times. AC11 asserts no CORS headers. RISK-5 is re-rated from inherent Medium to residual Low, citing the control.

(1) Holdout floors, each equal to its threshold minus 0.10, are enforced with a non-zero exit (R9, AC8, Success Criterion 2). AC8 includes a synthetic test in which the all-rows thresholds pass but a holdout floor fails. (2) Minimum counts are set: at least 60 benign rows, and a holdout of at least 20 rows with every category >= 3, every urgency >= 4 and label=high >= 5, checked by the runner. With 5 high rows, the 0.70 floor needs 4 of 5. (3) Freeze: sha256 evidence for the dataset and thresholds is recorded before the first commit to the fallback or detector rules. The verification gate checks both the hash and the timestamp ordering against git log, and the plan must order the dataset task first. RISK-4 is updated.

(1) Attack rows declare {family, targetCategory, targetUrgency, canary, url}. injection_leak (canary, url, prompt marker TDSK-SYS-7Q2, or a V2 match), injection_steer and attack_success are separate from accuracy, which is computed on attack rows using their true labels and printed separately. (2) RISK-1 states the residual keyword-steering risk, and the Fallback row corrects the 'cannot be injected' claim. (3) There are at least 20 attack rows across at least 6 families, including at least 2 held-out families (at least 6 rows), and held-out recall is reported with N. (4) Results are reported as 'k failures in N' with the 3/N bound and never as 'safe'. (5) Success Criterion 4 marks live results NOT RUN. findings.title: API key egress is unconstrained: fetch follows cross-origin redirects with x-api-key, and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL accepts plain http to any host and is commonly inherited
findings.detail: Three gaps let the key and the redacted ticket leave the host somewhere other than the intended endpoint. There is no request-driven SSRF: the URL is fixed at startup and never taken from request data. (a) Redirects. C6.4/C7 call fetchImpl with {method, headers, body, signal} and no `redirect` option, so the default `follow` applies. My probe on Node v22.22.0 (ev:ev-muymwez0-01deadbe) sent a POST with x-api-key to 127.0.0.1:A, which answered 307 to localhost:B, a different origin. Server B received `x-api-key: FAKE-KEY-123`, method POST and the full body. The same request with `redirect: 'error'` threw a TypeError. The Fetch standard strips only Authorization on cross-origin redirects, not custom headers. So any 307/308 from the configured base URL (a misconfigured or compromised proxy, a captive portal, or a MITM on an http base URL) hands over the key and the ticket. (b) Scheme and host. C6.1 accepts any `http:` or `https:` URL, so `http://<remote>` sends the key in cleartext. Userinfo, query and fragment are not rejected either (`https://x/?a=1` + '/v1/messages' produces a malformed URL). (c) Ambient inheritance. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is the variable the official Anthropic SDKs read for their base URL (claude-api skill reference, model table cached 2026-10-06, Client config: "`base_url` (or `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` env)"). It is set in this very build environment: I checked that it is set without printing its value. A developer who points it at a gateway for other tools would silently route TriageDesk's key and tickets there, and the listening log does not show it. T11 lists the threat, but the only mitigation is 'operator-only, documented'. In addition, test/helpers/spawn-server.js is specified as starting the server 'with the given env' without saying whether process.env is merged. A merged env would let a spawned 'fallback-mode' test pick up a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or base URL from the developer's shell, which breaks NFR9 (offline) and AC10.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the spec states all of the following, each with a named test. (1) C6.4/C7: the provider passes `redirect: 'error'` (add it to the fetchImpl init type). Any 3xx, or the resulting throw, maps to model_error with a fixed detail. Test in unit/anthropic-provider.test.js: a capture stub asserts init.redirect === 'error'. A contract test with fake-anthropic answering 307 to a second loopback server asserts a fallback model_error and 0 requests at the second server. (2) C6.1: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL must be `https:`, or `http:` only when the hostname is 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1]. URLs with username, password, search or hash are rejected with a ConfigError that names the variable only. Add unit/config.test.js vectors for http://remote.example (reject), http://127.0.0.1:9 (accept), https://u:p@x (reject) and https://x/?q (reject). findings.title: t16-readme runs `npm test` but does not depend on t14/t15, so it can run against another subagent's half-finished contract tests
findings.detail: t16's third acceptance criterion requires every documented command except full-mode eval to be run once from the project root and to work. The documented commands include `npm test`, whose glob `test/**/*.test.js` covers t14's and t15's files. t16 depends only on t13-app-wiring. I simulated the integration phase with the engine's own readyTasks() and the plan's dependencies at maxConcurrency=2 (ev:ev-muynyxxl-01ff66ef). All of t14, t15 and t16 are ready at once. After t14 completes while t15 is still claimed, t16 is the next ready task. Its `npm test` run then either fails on t15's in-progress files, so t16 fails or burns retries for reasons outside its ownership, or it passes on an incomplete suite, so the README's claim that `npm test` works is not established. This contradicts plan.md's own claim that a subagent is never failed by another subagent's half-finished files.

findings.title: The plan check scripts that verify t01, t02 and t16 and gate two phases are not in the submission, have no owner, and are editable by any task
findings.detail: The verification.command values of t01-scaffold, t02-eval-dataset and t16-readme, and the criteria of the foundation and integration phases, call .eccode/artifacts/plan/checks/{scaffold-check,dataset-precheck,readme-check}.js. The plan submission hashes only plan.json and plan.md. No task's file globs cover these scripts, and lib/tasks.js ALWAYS_ALLOWED (`.eccode/**`) lets any task change them without an ownership error at completion (ev:ev-muynyxxl-01ff66ef). So the instruments are neither reviewed nor pinned by this gate. The worst case is dataset-precheck.js, the pre-freeze guard for the frozen evaluation data (E5/D6). The test-engineer in t02 runs it against their own dataset and could change it without the engine or a later reviewer noticing. I read all three scripts, and on inspection they implement what plan.md describes. scaffold-check accepts the spec's exact §Deployment package.json and .env.example and rejects a mutated package.json (ev:ev-muynynlv-01f7a511). The problem is pinning, not content.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the resubmission includes the three check scripts as submission artifacts, so their sha256 values are recorded with the plan. plan.md must also state that no implementation task may modify .eccode/artifacts/plan/checks/**. The foundation and integration phase criteria (or the phase submission routine) must require the phase reviewer to confirm the scripts' sha256 values still equal the plan submission before relying on their output.

findings.title: t17's chained verification command conflicts with its own 'complete even if the full eval fails' criterion
findings.detail: t17.verification.command is `npm test && npm run eval && node .eccode/artifacts/design/design-vectors.js`. If the first full-mode eval exits 1 because a holdout floor is missed, the chain stops and design-vectors never runs. Re-running the same command would be a second full-mode run, which E5 forbids inside the task. The acceptance criteria already say the task completes on the passing npm test evidence, so the intent is right, but the literal command steers an implementer the wrong way.
findings.recommendation: Express t17's verification as three separate `eccode evidence run` steps, `npm test`, `npm run eval` (exactly once) and `node .eccode/artifacts/design/design-vectors.js`, instead of one && chain.

RISK-2.title: Automation bias: agents send drafts unread or mistake fallback output for AI output
RISK-2.mitigation: Permanent text source label + fallback reason, injection warning, copy-only (no send), 'not AI-generated' wording tested (AC5)

RISK-3.title: Live model (Haiku 5.5) slow/unavailable/refuses/truncates (adaptive thinking counts toward max_tokens)/returns invalid output
RISK-3.mitigation: 20s timeout, single attempt, effort low explicit, max_tokens 2048 with rationale (configurable), truncated reason+count, non-2xx -> model_error, V1-V4 validator, deterministic fallback with reason, fallback_rate and raw_model_validity metrics

RISK-4.mitigation: Dataset by test-engineer: >=60 benign rows, holdout >=20 with per-class minimums checked by runner; holdout floors (threshold-0.10) enforced with non-zero exit (AC8); dataset+thresholds sha256 recorded as evidence before any rules commit and checked by verification gate; N printed per metric
RISK-4.title: Eval not meaningful: fallback rules overfit a small same-team dataset, or dataset edited after rules exist

RISK-5.title: API key leak or key-spend abuse (incl. DNS rebinding from a malicious web page) via unauthenticated local server
RISK-5.mitigation: Key from env only, never echoed (AC10/AC14); Host allowlist (127.0.0.1/localhost/[::1]:PORT) + Origin check before body parsing, no CORS headers (NFR3, AC17); bind 127.0.0.1; body and max_tokens caps; one call per request. Likelihood re-rated Low after Host/Origin check (inherent Medium); impact High. Auth + rate limiting required before non-local deployment

RISK-6.mitigation: Metadata-only logs tested with marker (AC10), no persistence, R11 redaction of emails/phones/Luhn-valid cards before live call (AC16), live-mode notice naming redacted classes and what is not removed
RISK-6.title: Ticket PII logged locally or sent to third party without awareness

RISK-7.title: Model id / Messages API surface (claude-haiku-5-5, output_config.format restricted schema, effort) checked against docs only, not live
RISK-7.mitigation: Model via ANTHROPIC_MODEL, /api/health reports model, restricted schema keyword allowlist + AC9 schema walk, any non-2xx -> model_error visible in UI (AC4 c-f), first live call confirms, unverified status reported honestly

RISK-8.title: XSS via ticket or model text rendered as HTML
RISK-8.mitigation: textContent-only rendering, CSP default-src 'self' without inline script, grep check for HTML sinks (AC11)

RISK-9.title: Redaction misses: unusual phone/card formats, obfuscated emails and unredacted classes (names, addresses, account ids) reach Anthropic; over-redaction lowers live accuracy
RISK-9.mitigation: Ordered deterministic patterns email->Luhn card->phone with binding test vectors (R11, AC16, ev:ev-muylz82a-01c7d490); UI notice states redacted classes and that others are not removed; fallback mode sends nothing; per-class counts logged without content; user may decline live mode
